Thank you to the city of Saskatoon for proclaiming May as melanoma and skin cancer awareness month. My name is Natalie Richardson and I am the operations manager at Savior skin foundation.
I was diagnosed with stage three B melanoma the deadliest form of skin cancer in April of 2014 almost eight years ago to this day actually.
Fortunately, after multiple surgeries and immunotherapy treatments, I survived the ordeal and I'm currently living with no evidence of disease.
I'm passionate about my work with Savior skin and about this proclamation as the information within is critical to inform all Canadians in any way possible.
I have some statistics for you. Skin cancer is actually the most common of all cancers around the world.
There are more new cases of skin cancer diagnosed each year than the number of breast, prostate, lung and colon cancers combined.
And many people don't know one in six Canadians or in the 1990s will get skin cancer in their lifetimes.
Early detection and prevention is key to this type of cancer. No cancer, including melanoma, can ever be prevented with a hundred percent certainty.
But the good news with melanoma is that the risk factors are well known.
So steps can be taken to dramatically reduce the risk of developing this deadly disease.
Our skin is the largest organ of our body and it's the one organ that we can see and that our loved ones can see.
So to protect ourselves and and our loved ones, we can keep these important tips in mind.
Always have sunscreen with you so you can apply it whenever an unplanned outdoor activity arises.
Use a broad spectrum sunscreen with an SPF of at least 30 whenever you're outdoors, even on cloudy days.
We're protective clothing with long sleeves, hats and sunglasses.
Limit your sun exposure between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. for those who can. I've realized there are outdoor workers. This is a critical information for them as well across Canada.
Do not use tanning beds.
Check your skin head to toe every month for any unusual or changing moles or spots.
And we suggest that everyone should get a cancer related check up by a doctor including a full skin examination every three years between the ages of 20 and 40.
And annually for those 40 and older.
If you see something or find something suspicious on your skin, you should see your doctor immediately just to get a check out.
A little bit about Savior skin foundation.
We are a patient lead nonprofit organization founded by my boss mentor and best friend Kathy Bernard and her family in 2006.
We are dedicated to the fight against non melanoma and melanoma skin cancers and ocular melanoma through education advocacy and awareness initiatives across
Canada.
Savior skin provides a community of oncology, patient and caregiver support through the entire continuum of care from prevention and diagnosis to survivorship.
We are the leading melanoma organization in Canada and work with other patient advocacy groups in the US, Europe and Australia.
Thank you again for proclaiming May, melanoma awareness month and for helping us spread the word about this type of cancer.
